basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 3.' and it opens '(Vers. 3.) Et abiit in locum, quem dixit ei Deus, in die tertia. Notandum quod de Geraris'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 3.) Et abiit in locum, quem dixit ei Deus, in die tertia. Notandum quod de Geraris usque ad montem Moria, id est, sedem templi, iter dierum trium sit, et consequenter illuc die tertio pervenisse dicatur. Male igitur sentiunt quidam, Abraham illo tempore ad quercum habitasse Mambre: cum inde usque ad montem Moria, vix unius diei iter plenum sit.
